items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: at that time, when he played with us, he, he was copying

ctx.x: Now, the last time I saw Izzy, he was a, uh, uh, recording manager for Columbia Studios out there in California. Oh, really? He worked in the studios out there, and, he was, he was a legitimate man, see. But, uh, he tried to, I mean, he wasn't the greatest, the greatest style as far as I'm starting. No. I mean, he played, played a lot of good clarinet, and, and, he, he, he, at that time, when he played with us, he, he was copying, uh, I don't know, whether, who, who, who was a great clarinet player at that time,…

I just, when I compare a place like that with New Orleans, I wonder what it would be like to be on the lakefront, say, at the Spanish fort at, at Tokyo Gardens, in August. Uh, was it, how? It was wonderful. It was wonderful. It was cool, it was cool out, it was cool out there?
